mainEntity.name: How do I know your crew knows what it is doing in a clinical gym?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because training and competency validation are documented rather than assumed. Section I item B of the CDC Infection Prevention Checklist expects cleaning personnel to receive job-specific training and competency validation at hire and whenever procedures or products change. Our crews are trained on clean-to-dirty sequencing, color-coded microfiber, contact time discipline, and the specific products in your building, with records kept per person. Jeneva Thomas founded Dory's after 22 years of clinical experience, which is why the training is written around real findings rather than around a supply catalog.

mainEntity.name: Nobody here checks whether cleaning was done properly. Should we be?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and the absence of checking is itself a finding. Section I item D of the CDC Infection Prevention Checklist expects evidence that the clinic monitors and assesses whether cleaning is consistently and correctly performed. We build that in: dated service logs by zone, a supervisor audit on a defined interval using a written checklist tied to your own protocol, and a corrective-action note whenever something misses. You keep the record. The point is not to grade our crew for you, it is that you can show an assessor a monitoring process that exists on paper.

mainEntity.name: What documentation do I get for a CARF survey or a DPH review?

acceptedAnswer.text: The written cleaning and disinfection policy covering the gym, treatment tables, and shared equipment, with responsibility assigned line by line; the equipment inventory flagging items with no manufacturer reprocessing instructions; the product list with EPA registration numbers and label contact times; SDS sheets; per-person training and competency records; dated service logs; and supervisor audit results. That set answers Section I items A through D of the CDC Infection Prevention Checklist directly. Dory's carries $2 million in general liability and will name your clinic on the certificate.

What inspectors cite — and how we prevent it

Real, published regulatory findings — every citation links to its source.

CDC Infection Prevention Checklist for Outpatient Settings, Section II item A; CDC Core Practices 5f

Shared equipment reprocessed in a way the manufacturer never specified. CDC's position is that where no cleaning and disinfection instructions exist, the item is not suitable for multi-patient use.

CDC Infection Prevention Checklist for Outpatient Settings, Section II item B; CDC Core Practices 5b

Disinfectant wipes used with insufficient contact time — the surface dries before the label kill time, or the product is past shelf life or badly stored.

CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices 5f

Clean and soiled equipment stored together, with no physical separation to prevent cross-contamination.

Rehab Clinic Cleaning in Lancaster: the working detail

The surfaces we prioritise in Lancaster

  • Free weights, dumbbells and kettlebells
  • Resistance bands and handles
  • Waiting-room seating
  • Restroom fixtures
  • Door handles
  • Light switches

Our sequence, step by step

  1. Keep gym cloths separate from restroom cloths.
  2. Launder or replace reusable linens per the clinic's process — we do not take clinic linens off site unless contracted.
  3. Empty trash; sharps are rare but stay with the clinic's hauler if present.
  4. Damp-mop gym floors and vacuum carpeted areas.
  5. Log areas completed and any damaged equipment surfaces we notice.

A starting schedule

  • Restrooms and changing areas: daily or more often.
  • Waiting room: daily.
  • Periodic: equipment deep clean and high dusting.

Rehabilitation clinics are typically cleaned after the last appointment, since the gym is in use all day.

What you keep on file

  • Gym and treatment-room checklist
  • Product list with EPA registration numbers and contact times
  • Safety Data Sheets
  • Certificate of insurance

Before you sign with a cleaning company

  • Which products will you use on our table upholstery and mats?
  • Will you clean the free weights and cardio equipment every visit?
  • What will our staff still need to wipe between patients?

We answer each of these in writing after the free assessment.
